sections.source: FeetInspector's Spellblade Newbie Guide July 2025
lines: FeetInspector's Guide To Being The Best Newb You Can Be
Getting started:

Starting off in nights harbor, you'll want to go through the gate and hook a left. Ahead is a teleporter that will send you up to a four way split - to your left should be a sign pointing to the spellbinders area. That's where you'll find the guy mentioned in your note. Hand it in, listen to his dialogue, and start your newbie quest (very worthwhile).

The first step will have you collect singed skulls from decayed skeletons - you can find them outside west gate most reliably. You have to use either singe (your lvl 1 nuke) or Infuse Weapon: Flameburst (and it has to proc, so really just use singe for now). Hunting skellies will also give you some gear and cash, which you can sell and use to buy your spells. For now hunt this area, and when you've got some case and enough singed skulls head back to turn in the quest. Continue following the dialogue, run around town to the different turn-ins, and get ready to pause on that quest for a bit while you level as the next enemy group is a bit tougher.
Here are the most useful spells early on:
Singe
Strike
Infuse Weapon: Flameburst
Minor Spellshield
Kick (for interrupting casters that try to heal)
Unstable Barrier (absorbs damage, keeps you alive)

From here you just want to farm the newbie yard outside west gate then head into shaded dunes. Go left towards the coastline and check out the crocodiles, as they're a good source of early game XP. If you want armor hunt the dune scarabs and save their legs and carapaces for the beetle armor quest (check the wiki).
The rest of the info for those quests I'll leave to their individual guides

sections.title: Overview
sections.source: FeetInspector's Spellblade General Guide July 2025
lines: FeetInspector's General Spellblade Guide
What should I do to max my damage?
Grain of salt as this is still early days in the playtesting, but I found a few things that really kicked my damage up a notch.
Always have your infuse active. It can suck because it's low duration but don't forget to keep it up.
Wait for 5 stacks of infuse before casting. This let's you keep chopping and will instant-cast your next nuke.
Strike on cooldown.
Sub level ~10, I found using a big 2hander like a rusty scythe was more damage output than a fast weapon.

Once you get dual wield I highly recommend getting a faster main hand weapon (dagger, such as the mangler out of Ancient Crypt) and an offhand with a good damage-to-speed ratio. This increases your damage significantly as you get a lot of extra procs with a faster weapon, and at lvl 16 those procs start hitting for 44 damage. I have not tested a fast offhand so the good ratio advice is somewhat based on EQ knowledge. It might be better to have a faster offhand for more proc chances, but I'll have to test more in the future.
Make sure you're getting your buffs in group and callout if they fade. Haste is amazing. Strength buffs help you hit harder, and dex buffs help with your proc rate.
How do I solo?

This is a tough one. I solo'd a bit and it is doable, but the downtime can be significant. If you want to be a solo superstar there are better classes for it, but if you want to group and occasionally solo it can be done (at least up until lvl 20, I've gone no further yet) but bring bandages. Lots of bandages.

If you're committed, you'll want to keep your highest rank of unstable barrier up as much as possible. It absorbs damage and getting mana back is quicker than getting health back, so use it. Root-nuking is possible but a massive pain as our infuse procs tend to be stronger than our nukes at any given level.
I don't have much cash. What spells do I prioritize?
Infuse weapon spells (damage)
Spellshield
Unstable Barrier
Nukes
Root (buy at 14)
Invisibility (buy at 10)
Infuse weapon spells (slows)
Resists
This is assuming you also bought strike and kick. If you didn't go right now and buy them. Strike is good damage and kick is essential.
Other spells, such as shadowrift, are cool but don't really do a lot to help you group or solo.
What weapon type should I use

Great question! I touched on this earlier, but fast weapons in your mainhand seem to be best for triggering procs more frequently. More hits, more chances. As the procs are basically a free wizard nuke, it's the way to go. Daggers work well in that regard, though you'll often find yourself looking at a sweet new sword / axe / spear that dropped and thinking "hey this is way better" - in which case give it a shot! The important thing is to try and keep your weapon skills up. Nothing sucks like winning a cool sword and realizing your slashing skill is at 1 out of 95.

lines: Early Access Edition - Level 1-60 - Patch 0.30.x - October 2026
Maintained by SpectralAnubis.

sections.title: What Is a Spellblade?
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: The modern Spellblade is best described as a highly mobile magic swordsman. Your primary role is melee DPS, but your damage is not built only around white swings or only around spell casts. Your weapon attacks feed magical procs, your infusions alter what those procs do, and Conduit lets you cash an active infusion in for a stronger burst or utility effect.

The rework pushed the class away from the older “proc and hope” design. The current kit asks you to make more decisions: which infusion is active, whether to hold or conduct it, when to spend mana on a spell weave, when to Phase Strike, and when to back off with Seclusion or a defensive tool.

Role: Melee DPS with magical burst, mobility, light battlefield control, and limited group utility. In the current design, the class is at its best when a group lets it stay aggressive in melee while support classes cover mana, control, and survivability gaps.
Armor: Light armor. You can survive short periods of pressure, but you are not a true tank.
Combat feel: More active than most classic melee classes. Expect a higher action-per-minute playstyle when you are pushing the kit.

sections.title: Who Will Like the Class?
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Players who like hybrid melee/caster gameplay.
Players who enjoy timing procs, stance/infusion swaps, and short cooldowns.
Players who want mobility and the ability to reposition themselves or an enemy.
Players who do not mind watching mana while continuing to play in melee.
Players who like having several “good enough” answers instead of one button for every situation.

sections.title: Strengths
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Strong melee pressure with additional magic damage coming from infusion procs.
Excellent mobility for an old-school MMO melee class. Phase Strike is both a gap closer and a way to break stun/immobilize effects.
Three infusion identities let you lean toward damage, control, or defense depending on the fight.
Conduit gives meaningful burst/utility without needing a completely separate spell kit.
Useful defensive tools for surviving aggro spikes or solo pressure: Kinetic Ward, Seclusion, and later defensive cooldowns.
Can contribute to caster-heavy groups through Aura of the Arcane and magic-related debuffs.
Implosion becomes a very useful low-cost damage/debuff tool once acquired.

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Mana is a real resource. Overspending on nukes can leave you with little to do besides basic melee and melee abilities.
Light armor means mistakes and unwanted aggro hurt quickly.
The class can feel “busy.” Infusion management plus spell weaving is higher APM than the normal M&M sandwich-combat rhythm.
Reliable interrupts are not as straightforward as a traditional Kick. Electric effects can help, but do not treat the class as the group’s primary interrupter.
Telekinetic knockback can hurt your group if used carelessly. Moving the mob is not automatically good battlefield control.

Soloing is possible and the official kit includes solo tools, but the class is not being optimized in this guide around solo play. Adds and long fights can become ugly because both health and mana are taxed at the same time.
The class is stat hungry: Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, and survivability all matter.

sections.title: Available Races
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: The official Spellblade class list includes Deep Dwarf, Deep Elf, Dwarf, Gnome, High Elf, and Human. Deep Dwarf and High Elf are supported future Spellblade races but are not part of the EA launch race roster. Racial statistics and ability tuning can still change during Early Access.

Racial active system: racial actives/passives are automatically granted by race. They are not selected in place of your Major Combat trait. A Dwarf, for example, receives Stone Form and still chooses a Major Combat trait separately.

sections.title: Gnome - Offensive / Magic Specialist
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Highest known starting Intelligence (23) and Dexterity (22), giving excellent natural synergy with the Spellblade's magical and proc-based side.
Strong baseline for melee accuracy, infusion proc consistency, mana pool, spell damage, and Kinetic Ward scaling.
Gnomes automatically receive Slippery as a racial active. It is useful when movement-impairing effects threaten a light-armored melee character and does not consume the Major Combat trait choice.

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Lower Strength and Stamina than the sturdier choices.
More reliant on positioning, mobility, Kinetic Ward, and good threat management when a fight turns against you.

Recommendation: 5/5 for an arcane/proc-oriented build. Gnome has the strongest known DEX/INT starting package, but current STR testing means this should be treated as a specialization choice rather than proof of the highest overall DPS.

sections.title: Dwarf - Durable Battle Spellblade
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Best known starting Strength (19) while still retaining strong Dexterity (21), giving the class a very good physical foundation.
17 Stamina makes the Dwarf less fragile in melee than the Gnome without abandoning the important DEX/INT package.

Dwarves automatically receive Stone Form, a powerful emergency defensive racial that helps compensate for the Spellblade's light armor and lack of native healing. It does not consume the Major Combat trait choice.

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Lower Agility and Intelligence than the more specialized magical option.
Slightly less naturally specialized for the magical/proc half of the class than Gnome.
Recommendation: 5/5. Probably the best all-around recommendation. It gives up very little damage potential while improving the part of the class that most often gets you killed: surviving in melee.

sections.title: Human - Balanced / Flexible
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: 18 STR / 17 STA / 19 DEX / 19 INT provides a balanced hybrid base with no glaring statistical weakness.
Human is the easiest race to shape with the 10 bonus points because you are not correcting a major weakness or forced toward one obvious specialty.

Humans automatically receive Tenacity, an anti-incapacitate racial active that reinforces the race's flexible identity. Stun is no longer considered an Incapacitate, so Tenacity should not be treated as a stun cleanse.

sections.title: Weaknesses
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Does not lead the known Spellblade races in any of the most important class statistics.
Less Dexterity than Dwarf/Gnome and less Intelligence than Gnome.
Recommendation: 4/5. The safest choice for a player who wants the class - rather than the race - to define the final build.

sections.title: Deep Elf - Arcane / Evasive Hybrid
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Early Access launch: Yes. Deep Elf Spellblade starts at 16 STR / 15 STA / 19 DEX / 18 AGI / 22 INT / 17 WIS / 15 CHA before spending the 10 bonus attribute points. That gives Deep Elf the second-highest known Spellblade Intelligence behind Gnome and the highest Agility of the current launch choices, but only Human-level Dexterity and relatively low Strength/Stamina. This creates a natural arcane/evasive profile rather than the stronger physical baseline of Dwarf. Patch 0.30.0.0 also added an Ail'Vorith starter quest for Spellblade/Wizard, giving Deep Elf Spellblades a dedicated launch-path starting experience. The tradeoff is faction: Deep Elves begin Evil-aligned and are hostile to important surface factions, so travel, banking, vendors, and grouping logistics can be less convenient until players learn the faction routes.

Recommendation: 4/5. A strong thematic and mechanically viable arcane-leaning Spellblade, especially for players who value INT and AGI. On raw offensive starting stats, Gnome still has the cleaner DEX/INT package, while Dwarf remains the sturdier melee-forward option. Race/trait reworks during EA may change the final comparison.

sections.title: Deep Dwarf - Defensive Spellblade
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Early Access launch: No; planned for later. Deep Dwarf is an officially supported Spellblade race and is especially interesting as a future defensive/anti-control choice. Hardiness and historically associated defensive racials could create excellent synergy with a class that already uses Phase Strike, Kinetic Ward, and Seclusion to survive control and bad positioning.
Recommendation: Future option - stats TBD.

sections.title: High Elf - Arcane Spellblade
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Early Access launch: No; planned for later. High Elf is an officially supported Spellblade race. Thematically it should fit the arcane side of the class very well, but final public racial stats and racial abilities should be verified before calling it a min-max choice.
Recommendation: Future option - stats TBD.

sections.title: Recommended Traits
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Character creation gives you one Major Combat trait, one Minor Combat trait, one Major Non-Combat trait, and one Minor Non-Combat trait. Racial actives are granted separately. Treat the recommendations below as a starting point rather than a mandatory meta; Early Access tuning can change trait values and relative priorities.

sections.title: Major Combat Traits
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Current EA-prep recommendation: Strong or Dexterous are the cleanest general group-DPS choices, depending on how much accuracy/DEX your gear already provides. Intelligent becomes more attractive in magic-heavy, mana-supported groups. There is not enough evidence yet for a single universal Major Combat winner.
Dexterous - strong general-purpose choice when you want more melee consistency and do not yet feel comfortable with your hit rate against level-appropriate targets.

Intelligent - strong for a more magic-heavy build. INT supports mana, direct spell damage, infusion proc damage in current testing, and Kinetic Ward; its value rises when your group provides mana regeneration and Magic Resistance debuffs.

Strong - a very solid melee-forward option. Higher-level community testing currently shows STR improving white damage plus multiple core melee abilities, making it one of the strongest sustained-DPS investments.
Tough - viable for players who would rather patch the class's fragility than maximize damage.

Magic Resistant - an encounter-specific defensive choice. It can be valuable when hostile magic or dangerous control effects are common, but it is not a self-cleanse and is not automatically the best choice for a group-DPS build.

Current lean for group DPS: Strong / Dexterous first, Intelligent for magic-heavy or well-supported groups, with Magic Resistant and Tough as defensive alternatives. This is deliberately not a hard ranking; the class is still being tuned.

sections.title: Minor Combat Traits
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Channeler - strong hybrid choice if available to your race/class combination. Starting Channeling higher and improving its skill-up rate is unusually relevant to a caster who deliberately stands in melee.
Swordsman - best simple leveling choice. It accelerates Slashing progression and naturally fits the class's sword-based melee identity.
Warrior - a straightforward general combat option that improves Offense progression.
First-time player: Swordsman. Experienced player planning to weave spells aggressively in melee: Channeler.

sections.title: Major Non-Combat Traits
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Infravision - excellent general adventuring utility where available. Darkness in M&M is meaningful, so improved dungeon/night vision is not just flavor.
Master Artisan - excellent if crafting will be a serious part of the character.
Readiness - potentially very useful for a caster because of the extra Cantrip/memorization utility, if available to your Spellblade build.
Fast Metabolism - useful endurance tradeoff, but not something I would build the class around.
Iron Lungs - niche utility.
Slow Metabolism - not recommended for Spellblade if the endurance penalty remains, because endurance is already valuable to an active melee class.

sections.title: Minor Non-Combat Traits
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Medicine - my practical adventuring recommendation. Bind Wound is genuinely useful on a class with no native healing.
Bookworm - convenient and thematic for a magic swordsman, particularly if the extra spellbook remains part of the trait.
Tradeskill traits - Disenchanter, Herbalist, Alchemist, Blacksmith, Enchanter, Jewelcrafter, and similar options are perfectly reasonable if you already know which profession you intend to develop.
General recommendation: Medicine for adventuring, Bookworm for convenience/flavor, otherwise choose the tradeskill you actually plan to use.

sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Do not choose a deity purely for Spellblade min-maxing yet. Faith is still better treated as roleplay, faction, and character identity unless or until deity-specific mechanical bonuses become important enough to change a build. sections.title: Spellblade-Themed Recommendations
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Haradrel - the most obvious martial fit for a magically enhanced swordsman whose primary job is still melee combat.
Sorophal - a strong flavor choice for a character who treats swordplay and spellcraft as an art or disciplined craft.
Eltindra - surprisingly fitting for a highly mobile, teleporting, wandering Spellblade.
Vespyra - potentially the perfect thematic choice for an arcane-heavy Spellblade once available.
Agnostic - completely reasonable if you do not want religion to define the character.
For my character Durric specifically, Haradrel is the cleanest thematic fit: a Dwarven Spellblade built around STR/DEX/INT, Stone Form, weapon pressure, infusions, and Conduit under the God of War.

Character-creation takeaway: There is no single mandatory Spellblade race or trait package. Dwarf remains the strongest all-around physical/durable recommendation, Gnome has the strongest known DEX/INT offensive starting package, Human is the flexible middle ground, and Deep Elf is now a confirmed arcane/evasive option with 22 INT and 18 AGI but lower STR/STA. Starting stats matter most early; itemization and future racial/trait tuning can narrow or change these differences.

sections.title: Recommended Stat Mindset
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Strength - currently the safest general sustained-DPS investment for a melee-forward Spellblade. It improves the damage that is always happening: white attacks plus multiple weapon-ratio melee abilities.

Dexterity - important for connecting with melee attacks, especially as enemy level and avoidance rise. Community players have reported success around the mid-70s DEX in the high 30s, but there is no verified universal “75 DEX breakpoint.” Treat DEX as an accuracy requirement, not a magic number.

Intelligence - a meaningful secondary stat. Current testing shows INT increasing direct spell damage and infusion proc damage, while also supporting mana and Kinetic Ward. The question is not whether INT works; the open question is whether its current coefficients reward heavy stacking enough to beat STR for sustained DPS.

Stamina / survivability - still valuable because you are a light-armored melee class and will occasionally eat aggro. Defensive value matters, but this guide does not recommend sacrificing the class's group-DPS identity purely to optimize solo survival.

EA stat takeaway: Durric's mid-20s build naturally leaned STR-first, and higher-level community testing now supports that direction for sustained melee damage. Keep enough DEX to connect reliably, then treat INT as a real secondary stat whose value rises when you can afford more spell weaving. Do not read this as “INT is useless”; the evidence says the opposite - INT scales, but STR currently touches more of the always-on damage package.

sections.title: Community Testing: STR vs INT
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Pocah a forum community member posted a useful level-38 jewelry-swap test in the official Spellblade Deep Dive discussion. The test used light-green targets and swapped four jewelry pieces for +28 STR versus +28 INT. It is not a formal parse, but it is one of the cleaner public comparisons we have going into EA.
STR ~10%

What this suggests: STR currently wins more of the sustained melee package because it affects white damage and several core melee attacks. INT clearly scales the magical package, including the tested infusion proc, but those gains only dominate if you are actually casting often enough for them to matter.

sections.title: Why INT Still Matters
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Alikat a forum community member also reported testing roughly 30 INT versus about 160 INT using borrowed Wizard gear. Their offensive spells increased by roughly 26-28% depending on the ability, while Static Field showed no INT scaling in that test. That reinforces two points: INT does scale the class, but the return may feel modest relative to the amount of stat investment. Static Field should be treated as an ability-specific exception until more testing explains it.

The official Spellblade design also states that steady group play relies on procs for a significant portion of damage. That is why proc scaling matters even when an individual proc looks small: repeated activations turn small per-proc gains into part of the sustained damage engine.

sections.title: Adaptive Gearing
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Pocah's practical suggestion is to carry both STR-oriented and INT-oriented jewelry. Use the STR set when mana support is limited and your damage comes mostly from melee. Shift toward INT when an Enchanter/Bard or other group support lets you weave spells more aggressively and when Magic Resistance debuffs make those casts more reliable. Treat this as community-tested theorycraft, not established BIS.

sections.title: Community Tests Still Needed
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Isolate Telekinetic infusion proc scaling with STR versus INT.
Isolate Arcane/Electric Conduit scaling with INT rather than assuming it matches direct spells.
Compare equivalent-tier 2H versus dual wield using controlled weapons and the same buffs/target.
Map DEX versus hit rate across equal-, yellow-, and pink-con targets; do not assume a universal 75 DEX breakpoint.
Measure Maelstrom's real proc-frequency gain once its current aura bug is fixed.
Compare sustained damage with and without Bard/Enchanter mana support and resistance debuffs.

sections.title: The Heart of the Class: Infusions and Conduit
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Do not think of infusions as cosmetic weapon enchants. They are your combat stances. Each one changes what your weapon can proc, interacts with a matching spell, and changes what Conduit does. Learning when to stay in an infusion and when to spend it is the main Spellblade skill check.

sections.title: Why Procs Matter
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Procs are not flavor damage. The official Deep Dive says that in steady group play Spellblades rely on procs for a significant portion of their damage, and Maelstrom is designed to increase both attack speed and the chance to activate infusion effects. The current debate is therefore about how strongly those procs should scale - not whether they belong at the center of the class.

sections.title: Arcane Infusion
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Adds Magic damage procs to melee attacks.
Can apply Arcane Frailty, reducing the target’s Magic Resistance.
Reduces the mana cost of Arcane Spear while active.
Conduit turns the stored arcane energy into direct Magic damage.

Practical use: Arcane is a strong general-purpose stance when you want dependable magical damage or are working with other magic damage dealers. Arcane Conduit is straightforward free burst when timed well. Arcane Spear is useful for pulling, but spamming the line can become expensive.

sections.title: Electric Infusion
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Adds Electric damage procs to melee attacks.
Has a lesser chance to stun.
Reduces the mana cost of Discharge while active.
Electric Conduit deals Electric damage and adds a stun/arc effect.

Practical use: Electric is often the easiest infusion to live in during normal group DPS. The random stun can occasionally interrupt at the perfect time, and the matching Discharge line is generally easier to weave economically than repeatedly casting Arcane Spear.

sections.title: Telekinetic Infusion
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Adds Physical damage procs.
Can trigger Kinetic Siphon, reducing the target’s Movement Speed/Agility while increasing yours.
Reduces the mana cost of Kinetic Ward.
Telekinetic Conduit knocks the target back and immobilizes it.

Practical use: this is the situational stance. It is useful when you expect to take hits, need Kinetic Ward, want to create space, or want a root/knockback option. In groups, be deliberate: knocking a mob away from the tank or melee pile can create more problems than it solves.

sections.title: Conduit
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Conduit is the button that turns your current infusion into its payoff. The important part is not “press Conduit on cooldown.” The important part is asking what the fight needs. Arcane Conduit is damage. Electric Conduit is damage plus control. Telekinetic Conduit is positioning/control. Using Conduit also affects infusion availability, so pressing it commits you to a short-term plan.

Simple rule for new players: If you are not sure what to do, stay Electric or Arcane and learn the rhythm. Add aggressive infusion dancing after the rest of your melee rotation and mana management feel automatic.

sections.title: Static Field - Current Reality
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Static Field currently provides periodic Electric damage only. It does not currently lower Electric Resistance, stun, drain mana, or change effects with your active infusion. Those ideas are community design proposals, not live mechanics. In one high-INT beta test, Alikat reported no observable INT scaling on Static Field; that should be re-tested on the persistent EA build before treating it as a permanent rule.

sections.title: High-Level Utility and Defensive Milestones
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Deflection (30): one of the most interesting hybrid defensive buttons because a parry can also become an offensive infusion event.
Bend Gravity (35): niche, but useful for dangerous vertical travel, drops, and some dungeon geometry.
Magic Resistance (44): not a replacement for encounter-specific resist gear, but a useful self-buff as magical pressure rises.
Gate (51): finally gives the class meaningful self-travel back to bind. It is convenience and recovery utility, not a group port identity.

Maelstrom (57): the late-game offensive capstone. Attack speed plus more infusion activations should amplify the proc engine, although a current known bug can deactivate the active infusion when Maelstrom is used.

sections.title: Generic Utility Note
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Spellblade also retains generic magical utility such as dispel and protection/resistance tools. Community spell databases still contain some duplicate or cross-class indexing, so this guide does not assign an exact level to every generic utility spell until the persistent-server trainer data can be checked directly. For the wiki version, these can be filled in as players verify the live trainers.

sections.title: Leveling Roadmap: 1-60
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Important: Durric was personally tested through level 27 in Closed Beta. The level 30-60 section below is intentionally labeled as a working EA roadmap. It combines the current ability progression, official EA launch content, published zone ranges, and reports from players who tested higher levels. As soon as persistent-server routes and camps are proven, replace theory with actual experience.

sections.title: Levels 1-9: Learn the Hybrid Rhythm
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Stay in melee. Your spells supplement your weapon; they do not replace it.
Learn Arcane and Telekinetic interactions before trying to stance-swap constantly.
Use Arcane Spear as a pull/softener, then transition into melee.
Build muscle memory around Infused Slash and Phase Strike.
Treat mana as part of your damage budget; being empty when the next pull arrives is real downtime.

sections.title: Levels 10-17: Electric Comes Online
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Electric Infusion + Discharge gives you the easiest early sustained spell-weaving package.
Conduit should be a choice, not a reflex. Arcane = burst, Electric = damage/control, Telekinetic = space/control.
Seclusion at 14 is your first real threat-reset/survival correction and becomes increasingly important as your damage rises.
Keep Kinetic Ward available for bad pulls, soloing, or unavoidable return damage.

sections.title: Levels 18-24: Add Layers Without Breaking the Melee Core
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Implosion adds an avoidance debuff plus delayed Physical AoE.
Continue ranking Arcane Spear, Discharge, and Kinetic Ward, but do not assume the highest-rank nuke is always the best damage-per-mana choice.
Use Arcane or Electric as your normal offensive home; bring Telekinetic forward when the encounter actually needs its control/defensive tools.
At this stage, support quality begins to matter: mana regeneration and resistance debuffs can change how aggressively you cast.

sections.title: Levels 25-29: The Early Kit Becomes a Real Class
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Flurry I at 25 completes the early melee core.
Static Field I at 26 is a situational damage field, not a control/debuff field in the current build.
Implosion II arrives at 28.

Content direction: finish the useful portions of Tel Ekir (10-35), Caves of Irem, Fallen Pass rat caves/early groups, Glass Flats open flats (24-36), Keeper's Bight (18-35), and other level-appropriate launch camps.
This is a good range to stop thinking in terms of a fixed rotation and start thinking in terms of priorities: keep swinging, use melee cooldowns, then add magic according to mana/support.

sections.title: Levels 30-34: Deflection and the First Post-Beta Step
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Deflection + Infused Slash IV at 30 is the first big post-30 milestone. Deflection can turn incoming melee pressure into infusion activations through parries.
Discharge III arrives at 34.

Recommended launch content: Grain Cellar (30-35), Rothold entrance/early floors (~30-45 dungeon), Glass Flats highwaymen (31-41), Fallen Pass human/smuggler/plague camps, and the lower ends of Scarwood, Shallow Shoals, or Vale of Zintar.
For guild progression, this is where dungeon knowledge, clean assist discipline, and reliable CC/pulling begin to matter more than squeezing another few points of personal DPS.

sections.title: Levels 35-39: Utility Broadens, Magic Ranks Catch Up
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Bend Gravity (35), Arcane Spear IV (36), and Static Field II (38) arrive in this band.
Rothold should remain a major dungeon option; its developers described it as roughly level 30-45 content.
Other documented options include Glass Flats, Scarwood (28-47), Shallow Shoals (27-48), Vale of Zintar (18-50), and higher Fallen Pass camps.
Glinting Hollow begins around 38+, but its documented first-floor camps trend into the low 40s, so treat 38 as an entry point rather than an automatic XP destination.

sections.title: Levels 40-44: The Mid-Game Hybrid Is Fully Established
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Infused Slash V and Kinetic Ward IV arrive at 40; Implosion III at 42; Magic Resistance at 44.
At this point, keep a defensive/flex bar rather than trying to cram every spell into one permanent setup.
Continue Rothold through its useful range, then rotate through Scarwood, Shallow Shoals, Vale of Zintar, Fallen Pass, and Glinting Hollow (documented 41-47 internal camps).
Shaded Dunes also contains higher-level pockets around the 40 range, and Ail'Vorith has high-level city/guard content, though faction/access can make it impractical.

sections.title: Levels 45-49: Flurry II Changes the Weapon Conversation
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Flurry II at 45 attacks three times per equipped weapon. This is a major late-game melee/proc milestone and makes dual wield versus 2H much more important to test.
Discharge IV arrives at 46.
Finish the higher-value portions of Rothold, Glinting Hollow, Scarwood, Shallow Shoals, Vale, and Fallen Pass as mob con and camp efficiency allow.
Glass Flats Undead Keep Gatehouse is documented around 45-50 group content and is a natural bridge toward the 50s.
Do not declare dual wield the winner just because Flurry II creates more attack events; equivalent-tier parsing is still needed.

sections.title: Levels 50-54: High-End Launch Content Opens
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Infused Slash VI at 50; Gate at 51; Arcane Spear V and Static Field III at 52; Discharge V and Implosion IV at 54.

Fallen Watch becomes a serious high-end destination, but community reports describe it as punishing enough that even level 60 and strong gear matter. Treat it as progression content, not casual chain-pull XP.
Grimtide Sanctum is documented as 48+ with level-50 approaches, while Glass Flats has 51-53 group content at the Cultist Enclave.
Fallen Pass extends into the 50s, and other launch mini-dungeons/secrets may produce better routes once EA players map them.
This is the range where keeping Discharge V available can make sense even after VI exists later: beta testers found lower ranks easier to sustain without Bard/Enchanter mana support.

sections.title: Levels 55-60: Complete the Launch Kit
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Arcane Spear VI (56), Maelstrom (57), Discharge VI (58), Static Field IV (59), and Kinetic Ward V (60) complete the documented launch progression.
Maelstrom should push the class harder into its attack-speed/proc identity, but re-check the official known issue that can deactivate the active infusion on use.

Glass Flats has documented 58-60 group content at the Undead Keep Throne Room. Fallen Watch and Grimtide Sanctum are major high-level group/dungeon targets; raid and secret content will also shape the real 55-60 route.

At this stage the question is no longer “what buttons do I have?” but “how much magic can this group support without hurting sustained uptime?” Keep STR/DEX melee consistency as the floor and scale INT/spell usage with mana support and encounter demands.
The 55-60 section is the most provisional part of this guide. Replace these recommendations aggressively as EA guilds establish reliable camps, parses, and named progression.

sections.title: EA Zone Roadmap at a Glance
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Good bridge from the tested beta range into launch progression.
Dungeon/group fundamentals begin to matter more.
Use mob con and group composition rather than treating zone range as a hard requirement.
Broadest mid-game choice band.
Flurry II arrives at 45; excellent range for weapon testing.
Expect more punishing dungeon mechanics and resource pressure.
Most provisional route; current public mapping is incomplete.

sections.title: Current EA Identity: Group DPS First
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Spellblade can solo, and the official class write-up gives it tools for doing so. However, this guide evaluates the class primarily as a group melee-DPS specialist. The kit becomes much more effective when a tank controls positioning, a healer covers the risk of light armor, and support classes provide mana regeneration, crowd control, or Magic Resistance debuffs. That context also makes the proc-and-spell-weaving side of the class easier to sustain.

sections.title: Basic Group Flow
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Start in Arcane or Electric Infusion based on the target and your mana plan.
Let the tank establish control. Do not Phase Strike into a fresh pull just because the button is available.
Engage and maintain auto attacks while using Infused Slash, Phase Strike, and later Flurry.
Add Implosion when appropriate.
Weave Discharge or Arcane Spear when the mana cost is justified and the cast will not cost you more melee pressure than it adds.
Use Conduit when its payoff matters. Arcane for clean burst; Electric when stun/control is valuable; Telekinetic only when reposition/root is genuinely useful.
If you pull aggro, use Kinetic Ward if you must absorb hits, then Seclusion to reduce threat and create distance.
Re-enter with Phase Strike after the tank re-establishes control.

sections.title: Simple Damage Priority at Level 25
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: There is no perfect fixed rotation because infusions, mana, procs, and fight length matter. A practical priority is:
Keep attacking. White swings and infusion procs are free damage.
Flurry when available.
Use Infused Slash consistently.
Use Phase Strike for damage/positioning when it will not put you somewhere stupid.
Keep Implosion working when the debuff/damage is useful.
Conduit when you want the current infusion’s payoff.
Weave Discharge / Arcane Spear according to mana and group regeneration.

Community Electric example: Infused Strike -> Flurry -> Phase Strike -> weave 1-2 Discharges as mana permits -> repeat as cooldowns return. This is a practical rhythm, not a rigid rotation. Hold Phase Strike when you expect to need its positioning or stun/immobilize removal.

sections.title: High-Level Group Notes (30-60)
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Seclusion becomes more important, not less, as your gear and damage improve. High-level beta players reported pulling threat often enough that threat management belonged on the core bar.

Do not automatically cast the highest Discharge rank. A high-level beta tester reported using Discharge V for better sustain when Bard/Enchanter mana support was absent, then switching to the highest rank when support allowed it.
Deflection is both survival and proc pressure: a parry can trigger the active infusion, so the button is not purely defensive when melee pressure is incoming.
Static Field remains situational. It currently contributes only periodic Electric damage, so its value rises mainly when targets remain inside the field long enough to justify the slot.

Telekinetic remains best viewed as a toolbox stance in normal groups. Swap to it when Kinetic Ward, displacement, immobilize, or emergency peel matters - not because every pull requires equal time in every infusion.

By the 50s, group composition can change your damage plan dramatically. Mana regeneration and Magic Resistance debuffs make aggressive spell weaving much more sustainable; without them, your melee/proc engine must carry more of the load.

sections.title: Solo Play
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Solo Spellblade is possible, but it is not the optimization target of this guide. When you do solo, avoid trying to face-tank everything: open from range when it makes sense, commit to melee with a defensive plan ready, and create distance when the fight turns. Telekinetic tools, Kinetic Ward, Seclusion, and Phase Strike give you ways to manipulate a fight that a normal melee class does not have.
Soften the mob with Arcane Spear if the mana cost is reasonable.
Use Kinetic Ward before or during the dangerous portion of the fight.
Spend your best melee cooldowns while the target is controlled and you are healthy.
If the fight turns, Seclusion can create a reset window instead of forcing a bad face-tank.
Adds are the real danger. Spellblade does not have unlimited health, mana, or hard crowd control.

sections.title: Recommended Ability Bars by Milestone
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: These are practical starting bars, not mandatory rotations. M&M rewards changing utility for the encounter. The higher-level recommendations blend the official kit with reports from level-55+ beta Spellblade players.

Flurry I

sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Infused Slash VI (once available)
Flurry II

High-level community template: one level-55+ tester reported Implosion / Phase Strike / Infused Slash / Flurry / Seclusion / Kinetic Ward / Conduit as a reliable seven-button core, leaving roughly three flex slots for Discharge, Arcane Spear, Deflection, Static Field, dispel, and resistance/encounter utility. Treat that as a tested template, not a solved meta.

sections.title: Weapons
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Spellblade is not locked into one obvious weapon answer. Weapon ratio, available stats, dual-wield options, and how multi-swing abilities such as Flurry interact with your setup all matter. Going into EA, 2H versus dual wield remains an open testing question.
A strong two-handed weapon can produce satisfying large hits and simplifies gearing.

Dual wield can become attractive because multi-swing attacks such as Flurry create more individual weapon events. At higher ranks, that interaction may become more important, but it has not been cleanly proven to beat a high-ratio 2H weapon.
Do not chase attack speed only because older Spellblade designs favored fast proc weapons. The rework was specifically built to move away from flat-damage proc bias toward fast weapons.

At level 25 and during early EA progression, use the best overall weapon package you have rather than forcing a theoretical endgame setup. More attack events can smooth out misses, but that is a variance advantage - not proof of higher average DPS.

sections.title: Flurry II at Level 45
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Flurry II is the milestone that makes the late-game 2H-versus-dual-wield debate especially important: it performs three attacks per equipped weapon, and each attack can interact with the infusion system. Dual wield therefore creates more individual attack events, but a high-ratio two-hander concentrates more damage into each successful hit. More events can smooth variance and create more proc opportunities; they do not automatically prove higher average DPS. The guide should keep this unresolved until equivalent-tier weapons are parsed under controlled conditions.

sections.title: Gear Stats
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Strength: current general sustained melee damage priority.
Dexterity: accuracy and melee consistency; maintain enough to connect reliably rather than chasing an unverified breakpoint.
Intelligence: mana, direct spell damage, tested infusion proc damage, and Kinetic Ward scaling. Its value rises with mana support and resistance debuffs.
Stamina / HP / AC / useful resists: you are still standing in melee in light armor.

Beta gear examples used around the mid-20s included weapons such as Brawler’s Fist and Kazessthra’s Bane, but treat individual beta items as examples rather than mandatory progression. Itemization will continue to move, and a guide should not convince a new player that one named drop is required to make Spellblade work.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Playing like a Wizard: standing back and draining mana on nukes wastes the melee half of the class.
Playing like a Fighter: ignoring spells, procs, and infusions leaves a large part of your kit unused.
Using Conduit just because it is ready instead of because you want the effect.
Knocking mobs around with Telekinetic Conduit in a group without understanding the tank/CC plan.
Using Phase Strike automatically and teleporting into bad positioning, adds, or a target the group intends to crowd-control.
Spamming the highest-rank spell when a cheaper rank would sustain nearly the same kill speed.
Stacking only INT and assuming “magic swordsman” means caster stat first. Current testing shows INT works, but STR presently benefits more of the always-on melee damage package.
Ignoring Dexterity and then wondering why melee performance falls off against tougher targets.
Treating Kinetic Ward as permission to tank instead of an emergency/solo defensive tool.
Treating a community observation such as “75 DEX felt good” as a verified universal breakpoint.

Assuming Static Field has a debuff or control rider. In the current launch build it is a periodic Electric damage field only; any infusion-dependent field effects being discussed on the forums are design suggestions, not current mechanics.

Treating the level-30+ roadmap as proven. Post-30 recommendations in this edition are launch-build guidance until persistent EA groups establish the best camps, routes, and encounter-specific rotations.

sections.title: What Changed With the Rework?
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: The rework sharpened the Spellblade into a melee DPS class rather than a hybrid that drifted between proc-bot, caster, and off-tank. The biggest thematic changes are:
Infusions + Conduit are now the central combat system.
Arcane, Electric, and Telekinetic magic define the class; the older broader elemental identity was reduced.
Teleportation is treated as a combat mechanic through tools such as Phase Strike and Seclusion.
The old off-tank emphasis has been reduced. Kinetic Ward remains defensive, but the class’s official role is melee DPS.
The design attempts to reduce dependence on pure RNG and fast-weapon proc abuse by giving the player more active decisions.
The tradeoff is complexity: the new Spellblade can feel substantially busier than classic “sandwich combat.”

sections.title: My Read on the Class at Early Access Launch
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: The full 1-60 kit reinforces the same conclusion that emerged in the 20s: Spellblade is strongest when the melee engine remains the floor and the magic layer is added deliberately. The class does not need every spell on every pull. It needs consistent weapon pressure, enough Dexterity to connect, smart infusion choices, and mana discipline.

The late-game milestones make the class more complete. Flurry II at 45 dramatically increases the number of attack events available to a dual-wield setup, Gate at 51 adds meaningful self-travel, Maelstrom at 57 pushes the proc/attack-speed identity, and Kinetic Ward V at 60 gives the defensive line a true endgame rank. None of those changes the official role: you are still light-armored melee DPS, not a tank with spells.

The most important late-game tuning question may be resource support. High-level beta reports suggest Spellblade can produce excellent damage, but the amount of direct spell weaving you can sustain changes sharply depending on Bard/Enchanter mana support and resistance debuffs. That makes adaptive gearing and down-ranking damage spells legitimate tools rather than signs that the class is being played incorrectly.

My current expectation for EA is a STR-forward sustained melee base, enough DEX for reliable accuracy, and INT as a meaningful secondary that becomes more valuable as your group can support more magic. Telekinetic should remain a situational control/defensive stance in most groups; Arcane and Electric are the normal offensive homes.

Bottom line: the level-60 Spellblade looks less like a half-finished hybrid and more like a complete high-input melee DPS toolkit. The open questions are still balance and flow - mana efficiency, INT/proc coefficients, Conduit/infusion friction, Static Field value, and 2H versus dual wield - not whether the class has a coherent identity.

sections.title: Early Access Known Issues / Watch List
sections.source: SpectralAnubis's Spellblade Guide - EA Launch Edition October 2026
lines: Deep Elf starting Spellblade stats are now verified for the current EA build (16 STR / 15 STA / 19 DEX / 18 AGI / 22 INT / 17 WIS / 15 CHA). Racial actives/passives, trait availability, vision changes, and deity/faction restrictions should still be rechecked after the planned racial/trait rework and major EA patches.
Patch 0.30.x is the Early Access launch branch, not a final 1.0 balance state. Mana costs, coefficients, cooldowns, itemization, and infusion behavior can continue to change.
Official known issue: using Maelstrom currently deactivates the active infusion aura. Treat this as a bug, not intended rotation behavior.
Official known issue: Spellblade infusions can default to Telekinetic after zoning or reloading. Always verify your active infusion after a zone/reload.
Official known issue: the Infusion Conduit buff may fail to reduce cast time after zoning. Recheck after patches before building rotation assumptions around the buff.

Patch 0.30.0.0 added an Ail'Vorith starter quest for Spellblade/Wizard but did not include a dedicated Spellblade balance section, so the class is entering the final pre-launch stretch largely on the existing rework tuning.

Community feedback remains mixed on infusion stance-dancing and the downtime created by Conduit/infusion cooldown interactions. That is a design/tuning discussion, separate from the tracked bugs above.

Static Field correction: the live/launch-era spell line currently deals Electric damage only. One beta test reported no INT scaling; verify that again after EA patches before treating it as permanent behavior.

High-level progression watch: Flurry II (45), Maelstrom (57), and Kinetic Ward V (60) should be re-tested on persistent servers because they materially affect weapon choice, proc frequency, and defensive scaling.

sections.title: Using Glyphs
sections.source: Wizard Combos
lines: Casting Glyph: Mun, Glyph: Hil, Glyph: Nas, or Glyph: Dur adds a buff icon, setting up the spell to cast, lasting 15 seconds. Up to three glyphs can be cast per spell. Once ready, cast Spell Catalyst to begin casting the spell.

Note: When casting spells, you get the highest level version of the spell available in your spell book when cast, rather than the specific spell listed in the table. The spell must be available in your spell book.
